```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE,
                      fig.align="center", out.width="100%",
                      fig.width=10, fig.height=6, dpi=110)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(dplyr); library(ggplot2)})
DATA_DIR <- "../docs/global_analysis_data"
BR <- c(g = "#228b22", gd = "#176b17", gdd = "#0f4d0f", gold = "#b5791b",
        ink = "#1d2a1d", mut = "#566656", line = "#d6e4d6", bg = "#f3f8f3",
        charge = "#c0392b", warn = "#8a5a16")
source("R/counts.R")
cj2 <- readRDS(file.path(DATA_DIR, "climate_justice_headline_v2.rds"))
em  <- readRDS(file.path(DATA_DIR, "emergy_metrics.rds"))
n_cell_countries    <- cell_country_count()
n_canonical         <- canonical_burden_countries()
n_grid_cells        <- n_rows("cell_grid_wide.rds")
world_pop_bn        <- round(cj2$world_pop / 1e9, 1)
n_emergy_countries  <- nrow(em$country)
n_ember_countries   <- iso3_count("ember_by_fuel.rds")
transformity_ratio  <- round(max(em$country$transformity_sej_per_J, na.rm=TRUE) /
                              min(em$country$transformity_sej_per_J, na.rm=TRUE), 0)
ratio_b             <- round(cj2$ratio_b, 0)
low_acc_co2_share   <- round(sum(cj2$low_acc$cum_co2_mt) /
                              cj2$world_cum_co2_mt * 100, 2)
low_acc_pop_m       <- round(sum(cj2$low_acc$pop_owid) / 1e6, 0)
top_emit_co2_share  <- round(sum(cj2$top20_emit$cum_co2_mt) /
                              cj2$world_cum_co2_mt * 100, 1)
```

<div class="hero">
<div class="kicker">Global energy burden atlas</div>
<h1>Three lenses on the world's household energy</h1>
<p class="subtitle">
Household energy burden has never been comparably measured across most
of the world. We built the first open-code, open-data pipeline that
estimates it for `r n_cell_countries` countries and
`r format(n_grid_cells, big.mark=",")` grid cells covering
`r world_pop_bn`&nbsp;billion people. Three findings that no single
prior study surfaces: a <b>quality-of-energy</b> gap Odum's emergy
framework exposes, an <b>access + affordability + QoS</b> gap that
single-axis indicators miss, and a <b>climate-justice mismatch</b>
sharper than any prior estimate.
</p>
</div>

## Three findings

<div class="card-grid">

<div class="card">
<div class="kicker">Finding 1 — Emergy</div>
<h3>Grid quality varies `r transformity_ratio`× across `r n_ember_countries` countries</h3>
<p>Nuclear-heavy grids (France, Slovakia) deliver electricity with
~15× the emergy per joule of wind-heavy grids (Denmark, Germany).
Two grids with identical per-capita kWh can carry radically different
prior-emergy investment — invisible in CO<sub>2</sub> or kWh accounting.
Odum's framework separates <em>quality</em> from <em>quantity</em>.</p>
<p><a href="emergy.html">The Odum lens →</a></p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<div class="kicker">Finding 2 — Access + QoS</div>
<h3>"Connected" isn't "served"</h3>
<p>Global access to electricity is 91%; global access to clean cooking
fuel is 74%. Ontop of that, quality of service varies enormously —
outage frequency, voltage sag, tariff affordability. Households in
low-QoS grids are functionally under-served regardless of the binary
access statistic.</p>
<p><a href="access.html">Access, affordability, QoS →</a></p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<div class="kicker">Finding 3 — Climate justice</div>
<h3>The `r ratio_b`× per-capita CO<sub>2</sub> disparity</h3>
<p>The 20 least-electrified countries hold `r low_acc_pop_m`M people
(6% of humanity) and `r low_acc_co2_share`% of cumulative CO<sub>2</sub>
since 1750. The 20 largest historical emitters hold 4.8bn people and
`r top_emit_co2_share`%. Per-capita cumulative disparity is
approximately `r ratio_b`-fold.</p>
<p><a href="atlas.html#climate-justice-scatter">The climate-justice scatter →</a></p>
</div>

</div>

## Why publish this now

Each finding on its own has been sketched in prior work, but no
prior study combines all three at cell-level for
`r n_cell_countries` countries with fully open data + open code. The
combination reveals patterns that single-lens studies miss:

- **High-transformity + high-burden** — a country like South Africa
  (coal + nuclear grid, ~90k sej/J, 8% burden) is high-emergy AND
  high-burden — quality-adjusted energy is still expensive relative
  to income.
- **Low-transformity + low-CO~2~ + high-suppression** — wind-heavy
  small emitters (Portugal, Denmark) have low emergy per joule +
  low CO~2~ contribution, yet cells within them still show
  suppression pockets.
- **Climate-justice + emergy inversion** — the 20 countries most
  burdened by climate change (SSA + SAR) also receive lowest-
  transformity energy (biomass + low-access grids), a double
  penalty invisible when either lens is used alone.

<div class="callout">
<div class="callout-title">Caveats worth naming</div>
<p>The emergy computation inherits the country's grid mix onto every
cell (no cell-level fuel mix data exists at this scale). Cumulative
CO<sub>2</sub> is territorial-only (consumption-based would tighten
rather than loosen the disparity). Physics baseline uses global-average
building envelope. Full caveats in the <a href="global_analysis.pdf">
technical report</a>.</p>
</div>
